# Query a live track's EQ/filter target subtotal from an owned boundary snapshot

Parent #763. Astra xhigh requirements-first scope, 2026-09-13. Implementation baseline: merged main `cf9a620af4efa53672bfcdf48fc4757b5386b1bf`, including delivered #775 previews and #777 selected resident observations. Preserve both APIs. Paused #774 and prior catalog/projection briefs are not prerequisites. Luna max implements; Astra medium verifies frozen requirements and fixes concrete bugs without expanding scope.

## Required outcome and scope choice

Original #763 requires actual-graph declared linear EQ/filter composition, independent L/R, enable/bypass metadata, owner-correct rounded-word evaluation, honest target versus requested mode, and live snapshots carrying state identity and actual sample association. Full subscriptions/change suppression, shared jobs, spectra, common envelopes and joins also remain required, but need not precede a useful explicit live read.

**Approve one bounded end-to-end issue: an on-demand live track EQ/filter target query, including composition.** Copy one selected track's response state under the existing exclusive plan owner between completed render blocks; evaluate the immutable copy in #775's browser Worker or native/headless analysis code. The same capture traversal supplies the individual owners, so compose them in this issue rather than create another full delivery cycle for a single-EQ-only endpoint. One track per query and total-only composed output are sufficient. Existing #775 continues to supply explicit individual section previews.

No continuous snapshot publisher, new SPSC lane, subscription service, state mirror, full-session recompiler, second render engine, or standalone explicit-chain utility. No new live HPF/LPF commands: those cutoffs are currently `PreparedOnly`; capturing their actual prepared words is correct until actual plan replacement.

## User-visible contract

Provide `engine.queryTrackResponse({ trackId, grid, channels, responseLimits })` through browser and headless SDKs, plus native caller-buffer capture/evaluation. Routine naming follows existing conventions. The SDK method captures from its actual engine, then delegates numerical evaluation to the existing analysis module/Worker. It never accepts caller parameters as live state and never evaluates inside Worklet `process()` or its message handler.

Return the engine-generated frequency axis, selected owned L/R subtotal arrays, `mode: 'target'`, `meaning: 'eqFilterSubtotal'`, sample rate/floor, actual stable track and ordered member identities/configuration, an immutable state-snapshot identity and `capturedSample: bigint`. This is the stationary response of the targets that the owner held at capture; during a ramp it is not the transfer of the time-varying samples already rendered. Do not report `effectiveSample` unless its exact value is actually available. Keep #775's `requestedConfiguration` results unchanged.

Define capture precisely: after the previous successful render has returned and before the next block's queued controls are drained, at `PreparedRenderPlan::next_absolute_sample()`. Before any render, zero is the real initial boundary of the published plan, not a made-up application sample. An admitted but undrained command is absent from the snapshot, including a command queued for that next sample. Host failure/partially failed render refuses capture; do not stamp partially advanced DSP state with an unchanged successful clock.

Capture the entire selected chain in one exclusive-owner call. All included owners and bypass flags describe that same boundary. The worker reads only immutable copied state and never a plan pointer. Give each captured value a checked host-scoped u64 snapshot token; it identifies that immutable copy, not a new claim of a global engine clock or coefficient revision. Reuse #777's accepted current-host association/lifetime checks: close, failed reload, replacement or recreation invalidates pending old-host delivery. No changed effect inherits state by position. Native callers that use `RealtimePlanOwner` preserve the actual active `PlanEpoch`; the browser's current reload/recreate API must not invent one.

The result lists input filters, SIMD rack 1 effects, dynamic-rack effects and SIMD rack 2 effects in actual declared signal order. Include every owner declaring linear response support, including disabled/bypassed owners with identity semantics. Record excluded processors in place with native ID, stable slot/rack and explicit unavailable reason; do not silently make a compressor identity or call an unknown processor nonlinear. Fixed exclusions are polarity, trim/alignment delay, fader/mute, matrix/pan, routing/mixing/sends/sidechains/PDC and downstream processing. Always call the result an EQ/filter subtotal.

## Concrete reuse and minimal new code

1. **Copy the owners' actual words.** `parametric-eq/src/lib.rs::Channel::target_words` already holds the six rounded f32 target words for each of four sections; `targets` holds independent enable/kind data. Add a small owner-controlled immutable snapshot constructor and worker-side preparation from that snapshot beside `parametric-eq/src/response.rs`. It copies words/flags; it does not design coefficients during capture. The scalar and bank snapshot hooks share the existing `PreparedParametricEq<L,W>` implementation. Live bypass comes from `EffectControlLane::bypassed()`, not the processor's initial metadata; console-free instances use their prepared bypass. A collapsed lane must preserve its correct dual-mono target semantics.
2. **Capture the actual input owner.** `builtins::InputStage`/`InputBuiltins` and `BuiltinInputBank` retain the rounded HPF/LPF words. Add the same small immutable input-response snapshot beside `filter_response.rs`; forward the lane copy through `builtins-compiler`'s existing scalar `InputProcessor`/`ConsoleInputProcessor` and builtin bank owner. HPF/LPF do not currently change through live controls; trim/polarity changes cannot affect this subtotal. Do not reconstruct these words using EQ's designer or a caller/session parameter mirror.
3. **Reach the existing runtime owners.** Add only the narrow caller-buffer snapshot-copy hooks needed on existing effect/graph/rack dispatch traits, defaulting to typed unavailable for unsupported owners. `PreparedPlanExecutor` is in `engine`, which has no production dependencies and cannot depend back on effect-contract/graph; keep that seam to bounded identity/payload copying, not effect DSP types. `GraphExecutor`/`runtime::RuntimeUnit::{Op,Bank}` dispatches to the real scalar processor or `BankChain` stage/lane. Existing `PreparedNativeEffect`/bank state snapshots omit some nonautomatable EQ configuration and do not serialize exact target words, so do not pretend their current full-state payload alone supplies the needed target snapshot. Use the small dedicated owner hook instead of a general state serialization redesign.
4. **Retain only indispensable lookup metadata.** `RuntimeOp` currently drops graph node IDs; `UnitIdentity` retains track names but not effect-slot identities. During existing graph lowering, retain a compact stable-node -> runtime unit/stage/lane mapping (or extend the existing identity metadata equivalently). `GraphPreparedEffectBank.members`, `GraphNodeId::Effect`, `EffectNodeId` and `program`/typed chain construction already supply the authority. Preserve actual input/SIMD1/dynamic/SIMD2 order from the compiled chain, never lexical IDs or hoisted bank execution order. Do not recompile a session or restore #774's independent catalog/handle provider. Charge this real metadata in existing graph preparation/resource estimates; reuse existing compile caps and bounded request limits. Capture introduces no retained DSP copies or per-block work.
5. **Compose off render.** Reuse the accepted owner transfer evaluator and #775 `generate_response_grid`. Add only an unfloored per-frequency f64 magnitude access needed by the composer, with an explicit owner capability; ordinary floored response outputs remain unchanged. For each lane accumulate positive magnitudes in f64 log space (`sum 20*math::log10(m)`), with an absorbing exact-zero flag, then floor once at -120 dB and convert once to f32. This avoids intermediate floor, underflow and overflow along admitted long chains. Reject negative/NaN/infinite magnitudes even after a prior zero; validate both lanes and every owner before publishing any output. No JS curve math, generic transfer solver, phase/matrix/nonlinear estimate or optimization.
6. **Reuse the working endpoint.** Add one bounded snapshot request/reply on the existing live-host/control staging path, then extend #775's analysis-only Wasm bridge and `ResponsePreviewModule`/response Worker to evaluate this captured snapshot plus grid. The Worklet handler only copies owner data/metadata under exclusive ownership; no coefficient preparation, logarithm, curve evaluation or second boot. Browser transfers immutable snapshot bytes to the existing Worker and returns owned arrays; headless captures between explicit render calls and calls the same Rust evaluator. #777's stable-selection/current-owner conventions and existing generated ABI/types/error plumbing remain the host authority. No general remote protocol or new worker framework.

Likely touched production paths: owner response modules plus their small capture methods; `effect-contract/src/{lib,response}.rs`; `engine/src/realtime/plan.rs`; `graph/src/{lib,runtime}.rs` and its existing resource estimate; `rack/src/lib.rs`; builtin compiler adapters; `host-core/src/{lib,response}.rs`; `host-web/src/{lib,ffi}.rs`; existing shipped Worklet/host message adapter; SDK core/browser/headless response and engine entry points; existing metadata/ABI generators/assets. This is one capture/evaluation feature across existing owners, not permission to refactor each subsystem. No new package/dependency beyond existing portable math already present. Keep all public layouts compatible except additive V1 surfaces.

## Bounds, identity and idle behavior

One active capture/evaluation request per owning SDK path; no queue/history/cache. Bound selected-chain items (including exclusions), snapshot bytes, output/grid points and total result bytes with checked arithmetic before work/publication. Source counts are constrained by existing configured resources, never a compiled track ceiling. Native owner capture copies into caller-provided storage without allocations/frees/locks; a native host schedules that call on the plan-owning thread between blocks and passes only the completed snapshot to its worker. Never borrow the plan from a control/worker thread while render owns it. No request means no capture, evaluation or traffic; no render-loop polling or notification is added.

A snapshot is immutable for its whole worker lifetime; one pending request cannot observe mixed replacement plans or reused buffers. Output arrays remain owned after subsequent queries/reloads/close. Typed refusal covers missing/changed track, unsupported required owner snapshot, invalid grid/fields, capacity, malformed snapshot and numerical failure. A failed member fails the whole subtotal. Static exclusions and absence of an applicable linear provider remain descriptive, not failures pretending to be unity.

The snapshot token plus actual host association identifies the complete captured state; no caller can relabel arbitrary bytes as live. The initial browser method is an explicit read, not a subscribed stream. Change-driven recomputation, identical-result suppression, cadence, shared jobs and stream-specific epochs/loss remain the next common-live-service obligation inside #763, not a claim made by this query.

## Few required gates and delivery

- **Actual state and time:** queue asymmetric EQ edits/bypass, capture before drain (old state), render, capture again (new target) and compare captured target words with the owner. Exercise a ramp, scalar/tail and representative bank/mono-collapse paths, prepared HPF/LPF, and capture after a failed render. Prove capture/query leaves audio and DSP state bit-identical. One test above 2^53 covers capture sample/token.
- **Composition/identity:** a real prepared track with differently named slots in all three racks and an excluded compressor proves actual membership/order. Compare composed output with the independent existing realized-recurrence oracle, including a deep cut followed by gain that would expose early flooring; zero/nonfinite cases and L/R/bypass. Use the existing owner oracle/PCM fixtures and four launch rates; no new corpus or benchmark framework. Same-position replacement/failed reload cannot return the old track's snapshot as current.
- **Real SDK and resources:** actual headless and Chromium/Firefox/WebKit query captures the real host, evaluates in the shipped Worker and returns matching finite axes/subtotals/metadata. Include bounded member/result refusal, pending close/worker error and stable owned arrays. Existing resource/ABI/generated/type/realtime/callgraph gates remain; Worklet capture must not invoke analysis math or boot another engine. Keep #775 preview and #777 resident read regressions passing.

Use frequent compiling local checkpoints for owner/capture/wiring work, but one coherent endpoint candidate/qualification boundary. Run focused checks while developing and the existing official artifact/resource/package/three-browser gates once the path works; preserve raw evidence and existing fail-closed report/discovery checks. No optimization or descriptive timing here. Astra medium verifies frozen requirements, actionable bugs and false claims; optional improvements/frameworks/exhaustive hardening are follow-ups. Luna max implements; root owns checkpoints, remote delivery and issue state; existing attempt limits apply.

If implementation discovers that the runtime identity/capture path cannot fit the bounded issue, stop before adding a second architecture. The fallback split is two **usable SDK outcomes**: live named-owner target queries through the same snapshot route, then actual-track subtotal/input-filter integration. Neither a raw-word primitive nor a lookup catalog closes a product issue. Prefer the combined slice above because lookup/capture is the dominant common work and composition is a small evaluator over it.

## Parent checklist stays binding

Still required after this query: generic selective subscriptions/update/read/close, identical-job sharing, effective admission/defaults, bounded state-change delivery and last-close disarm; full engine/plan/state/content/publication/loss envelopes; required post-input/post-matrix/final-output spectra with FFT/window/normalization/smoothing/gap/underrun behavior; native/headless pump and browser SAB/qualified pooled fallback; packed remote vectors, bounded sample join, integrated examples/docs/resource evidence and the one frozen descriptive comparison. #775 requested preview and #777 per-effect resident reads remain delivered capabilities. Only the parent's explicit later allowances (frozen-word mode, arbitrary effect taps, phase/group delay/nonlinear estimates, device-clock mapping and extended research/optimization) stay outside this first live-query scope.
